Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)
• 31-year-old man with 4-day history of intensely pruritic, sore, dry, cracked rash on chest, hands, and flexural elbows. No systemic symptoms. Past eczema.  
• Likely atopic dermatitis flare; allergic/irritant contact dermatitis also considered; scabies less likely but keep in differential.  
• Plan:  
  – Prescribe higher-potency topical corticosteroid (name/dose/route/frequency not documented).  
  – Prescribe emollient for bath/shower use; instruct regular application for 7–10 days.  
  – Prescribe non-sedating antihistamine (Fexofenadine; dose/frequency not documented).  
  – Advise diary of potential triggers (detergents, clothing, soaps).  
  – Follow-up in 1 week if no improvement or sooner if worsening.

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx):
1. Atopic dermatitis (eczema) flare – High likelihood: prior history, flexural involvement, dry cracked skin, intense pruritus, absence of systemic features.  
2. Allergic/irritant contact dermatitis – Moderate likelihood: acute onset, distribution includes exposed areas; no clear trigger identified.  
3. Scabies infestation – Low to moderate likelihood: severe itch, hand involvement, shared living space; no burrows or contact symptoms reported.
